properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check (comparing every 'trusted' parcel's committed pixel bbox against a fresh color-detected bbox) found this block's committed shape only ~110px wide against the diagram's real ~180px width, and extended noticeably too far south. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [105,64,115], '50ft Max') in a tight crop, connected-component labeled it, and extracted its precise contour (OpenCV) -- a clean pentagon (a rectangle with its SE corner cut at an angle) at pixel (1677,734), (1677,907), (1757,907), (1857,883), (1857,734). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. New area (~0.71 acres) is noticeably larger than the old (wrong, narrow) trace. Confirmed zero overlap with E1, E3, or the waterfront open space corridor; still overlaps Elevation Sky Park by ~1133 m2 (an already-documented, expected overlap given ESP's own low-confidence placement -- see that file). CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (found via join_approximate.py's new MAJOR CLIP warning, prompted by user-flagged issues elsewhere): confirmed via direct satellite comparison that this block's north edge sits on real, currently-paved road pavement (a real street/driveway visible with clear edges near the shoreline), not vacant land -- 37% of this block's area was inside the buffered real-street layer. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer, same pattern already used for Parcels D/E1/H1/H2; area dropped from ~2,883 to ~1,807 sq m. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: Building 14's footprint above is under legacy id mblr SF4052001 / blklot 4052001, which DataSF retired on 2018-10-02 (acdm-wktn; 21 footprints carry that id), so the id does not by itself identify Building 14 and no cited source ties them. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.'; accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel; E4 is in any case excluded from the developer's option). The block has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address); this hand-traced block overlaps mostly active lot 4052011 (about 77%) and 4052010 (about 15%) in that layer, which is only an overlay of approximate geometry, not an identification, and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008. No source read describes the block's current ground condition. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. E4 lies within the 28-Acre Site, whose developer is Brookfield's affiliate FC Pier 70, LLC (Port Items 9B and 12B), and DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows most of the site's re-mapped lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07) with no street address. The earlier statement that the site has not been subdivided per the masterplan's named parcels is withdrawn (named parcels have lots: Port Item 12B gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008); this block's own lot has not been identified, so this file uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel; E4 is in any case excluded from the developer's option). The block has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address); this hand-traced block overlaps mostly active lot 4052011 (about 77%) and 4052010 (about 15%) in that layer, which is only an overlay of approximate geometry, not an identification, and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008. No source read describes the block's current ground condition. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see the mapping log) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. E4 lies within the 28-Acre Site, whose developer is Brookfield's affiliate FC Pier 70, LLC (Port Items 9B and 12B), and DataSF's Assessor layer shows most of the site's re-mapped lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07) with no street address. The earlier statement that the site has not been subdivided per the masterplan's named parcels is withdrawn (named parcels have lots: Port Item 12B gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008); this block's own lot has not been identified, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: The D4D's land-use designation for E4 is Retail, Arts and Light Industrial (Figure 2.1.1), with office uses permitted in Building 12 and E4 except on the ground floor, and residential not permitted on E4 (Table 2.1.1) -- not residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) calls it 'the arts building parcel (Parcel E4)' and lists it among the parcels excluded from the developer's standard option under the DDA. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. Port Item 11A (2026) proposes to allow residential use on E4 if an arts facility proves infeasible. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see the accuracy caveat.
